clue.text: Terrorists, overthrowing Bulgarian rulers

indicators.note: overthrowing suggests turning things upside down, so the letters of the two following words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Insurgents topple the rulers of Bulgaria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrowing' reads as the terrorists' action, but it signals an anagram of BULGARIAN RULERS.
explanation.definitionFit: City-based irregular fighters using violence are commonly described as terrorists, a near synonym.

clue.text: Awkward one — hard, and extremely tricky

parts.note: UN is a dialect form of one, as in 'a good un'
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
taken as written

indicators.note: extremely keeps only the extreme end of the word tricky, cutting away everything before its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone clumsy is described as hard and very tricky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'tricky', but it leaves only that word's last letter, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking manual skill is clumsy, so the word is a straightforward synonym for awkward.

clue.text: Snatches purses containing pounds

indicators.note: containing tells us the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: purses are small bags for money
L (from Latin libra) is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A thief grabs purses full of money.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to blag is to steal or rob, so blags means snatches.

clue.text: Vegetarian food freak allowed to swallow a portion

indicators.note: to swallow means the pair of words around it take another piece into their middle

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or freak, as in health nut
let means allowed
a cut is a share or portion

explanation.surface: A health-food enthusiast is permitted to eat a helping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freak' suggests something odd, but here it means an enthusiast, as in a fitness freak.
explanation.definitionFit: A patty of chopped nuts shaped like a meat cutlet is a classic vegetarian dish.

clue.text: Drug addict, one reflects, off his head

indicators.note: off his head tells us to drop the first letter, the head, of the word found

parts.note: a muser is someone who reflects or ponders

explanation.surface: An addict, thinking it over, is out of his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off his head' looks like slang for high, but it removes the first letter of MUSER.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is a common slang term for someone who takes illegal drugs.

clue.text: Someone going back to work on a painting?

parts.note: RE means on or concerning, as in business letters
a Turner is a painting by J. M. W. Turner, the English landscape artist

explanation.surface: Is an art restorer returning to work on a picture?
explanation.walkthrough: 'a painting' is a Turner, the English artist's work.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who rejoins the workforce after a break is called a returner.

clue.text: Cultured Indian doing time?

definitions.meaning: the Inca civilisation of Peru was highly advanced, so an adjective or member of it is a cultured Indian
split as ..., being in the can, slang for in prison

explanation.surface: Was a sophisticated native American serving a prison sentence?
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Inca people of Peru built a sophisticated civilisation; can is slang for prison.

clue.text: A lone cur's in trouble for thieving

indicators.note: in trouble means the letters are in a mess and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written, the S of cur's included

explanation.surface: A stray dog alone gets into trouble for stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is theft, so the adjective formed from it means given to stealing.

clue.text: Place swamped by great wave making splash

indicators.note: swamped by means the first piece is engulfed by the second

parts.note: a surge is a great wave or swell
PL is the abbreviation for place in addresses

explanation.surface: A town is flooded by a huge wave with a mighty splash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splash' is spending, as in splashing out, not water.
explanation.definitionFit: To splurge is to spend lavishly, which is what splashing out money means.

clue.text: Being most cordial, twice try to accommodate one

parts.note: try is used twice: to hear a case in court is to try it

indicators.note: to accommodate means the second try makes room inside itself for another piece

parts.note: the second use: to test something is to try it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A host trying hard to fit in a guest is very friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' means the word 'try' gives two different synonyms, HEAR then TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty means warm and cordial, so the superlative means being most cordial.

clue.text: A Beethoven symphony, not. hard rock, perhaps

indicators.note: not means the following item is left out of the word

parts.note: the Choral is the nickname of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony

explanation.surface: A Beethoven symphony is not hard rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard rock' looks like a music genre, but 'not hard' removes the H and 'rock, perhaps' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral forms reefs of hard limestone, so it is an example of a rock.

clue.text: Lots of food, but no drink for a drunkard

indicators.note: for a drunkard means as slurred by someone drunk, so the S comes out as SH

parts.note: a sup is a drink, so no drink is no sup

explanation.surface: Plenty to eat, but nothing for a heavy drinker to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A drunk slurs 'no sup' into something sounding like a big meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosh-up is British slang for a large, hearty meal.

clue.text: The splendour of France, Greece and half of Europe

parts.note: GR is the international code for Greece
taken as written

indicators.note: half of takes the first three letters of the six in Europe

explanation.surface: The glory of France, Greece and much of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The splendour of France' is the definition: the word is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandeur is a French borrowing meaning magnificence or splendour.

clue.text: At last ferry's in good time not such a frequent event!

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word ferry

parts.note: early means in good time

explanation.surface: Finally the ferry arrives on time, which is rare!
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' reads as finally, but it takes only the last letter, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening once a year occurs only annually, so it is not a frequent event.

clue.text: This Greek was just one involved in terrible disaster

indicators.note: involved in means the item is placed among the other letters
terrible signals that the word disaster is mangled into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Greek with a just reputation was caught up in a calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside an anagram of DISASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: This Athenian statesman was famously nicknamed 'the Just'.

clue.text: College in financial difficulties, headed by retired politician

indicators.note: headed by means the other piece goes first
retired means withdrawn or drawn back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an MEP is a Member of the European Parliament
broke means having no money

explanation.surface: A college is short of money and run by a former politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' reverses MEP to PEM.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of colleges at both Oxford and Cambridge.

clue.text: Gasbag beginning to babble afterwards, about female

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of babble
about means the word goes around the next piece

parts.note: later means afterwards
her is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: A windbag starts to prattle afterwards about a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The page splits 'afterwards' across a line break, which is why the scanned text came out garbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who talks on and on foolishly is a gasbag, a synonym.

clue.text: Self-made southerner prepared exams during lessons regularly

indicators.note: during means one piece is placed within the other
regularly takes every other letter of lessons
prepared means made ready, so the word exams is reworked

explanation.surface: A self-made man revised for his exams during his classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes every other letter of 'lessons'; 'prepared' rearranges 'exams'. Essex Man is a British stereotype of the brash, self-made, upwardly mobile voter from Essex, east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The label describes a newly prosperous working-class man from south-east England.

clue.text: Means to identify allergic reaction, starting from scratch

definitions.text: Means to identify allergic reaction, starting from scratch

parts.words: Means to identify allergic reaction, starting from scratch
parts.note: a medical check for allergies where the doctor scratches or pricks the surface of the body, so it literally starts from a scratch

explanation.surface: A diagnosis for allergies begins from nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Allergists apply allergens to small scratches on the body to see which cause a reaction.

clue.text: Bird caused dispute, over noise?

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to spar is to argue or dispute
a row is a loud noise or din

explanation.surface: Did a bird cause an argument about the racket?
explanation.definitionFit: A small brown songbird common in towns, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Cab given order to follow German

indicators.note: to follow means the first piece comes after the second

parts.note: Hans is a typical German man's name
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A taxi is ordered to follow a German.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage for hire, the original London cab.

clue.text: King's number is up during protest

indicators.note: during means placed inside the other word

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration

indicators.note: is up in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: The king's time is up during a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number is up' reads as the idiom for doom, but 'is up' turns the abbreviation for number upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is a sovereign ruler, of whom a king is one.

clue.text: One charges minor attorney endless cash

parts.note: Att. is a short form of attorney, minor meaning cut down

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: ackers is British slang for money

explanation.surface: A junior lawyer seeks unlimited money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' is rushing at, not legal or financial charges.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who charges at others assaults them, so one who charges is an assailant.

clue.text: Heroin added in another drug could make you gag

indicators.note: added in means the first item goes inside the other

parts.note: coke is slang for cocaine
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Heroin mixed with another drug could make you retch.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to retch or struggle for breath, a synonym.

clue.text: Contribute feature about parking on island

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the others

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after

explanation.surface: Pay towards a car park on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature' suggests an article or attraction, but here it is a part of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: To chip in is an idiom for adding one's share of money or help.

clue.text: Work of art that's secured by school's fund raisers

indicators.note: secured by means held inside the next piece

parts.note: the PTA, the Parent-Teacher Association, raises money for schools
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A painting is acquired through fundraising by the parents at a school.
explanation.definitionFit: A pieta is a sculpture or painting of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ.

clue.text: Welshman's loud colours

indicators.note: loud means spoken out, signalling a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name, so Dai's

explanation.surface: A Welshman's garish colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loud' looks like it describes the colours, but it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyes are substances used to colour fabric, so they are colours.

clue.text: Travelled round on show

parts.note: rode means travelled on horseback
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone went round to a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a public show of cowboy skills.

clue.text: Organ kept by Mr Porter the composer

indicators.note: kept by means held inside

parts.note: taken as the abbreviation MR
the eye is an organ
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: An organ is owned by Mr Porter, the composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr Porter' looks like a name, but Porter is beer. Giacomo Meyerbeer was a German opera composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Meyerbeer was a nineteenth-century German opera composer.

clue.text: It's useless, so to speak

parts.note: speaking to no effect: to talk in vain, so to speak literally means talking

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to talk or argue to no purpose, so speaking is useless.
